sections.title: MLA Independent Study
sections.description: Students will begin the course by examining some attempts by classic nature writers and natural historians to understand and depict ecological realities, and will then turn to the response of contemporary writers (and other artists) to growing environmental crisis and the disappearance of the natural world. Readings will be supplemented by material drawn from advertising, television, and other sources (outdoor magazines, for example). The hope is that students will acquaint themselves with natural history as a literary form, explore the importance of concepts of natural to other forms of literature like the novel, and come to some understanding of the impact of environmental issues on the imagination. Readings may include: Emerson's "Nature"; and selections from Thoreau; Marjorie Kennan Rawling's Cross Creek,essays on culture and agriculture by Wendell Berry and Michael Pollan; Graham Swift's Waterland; Leslie Marmon Silko's Ceremony, essays by Martin Heidegger, Andrew Ross, Fredric Jameson, and Bill Mckibben; Don DeLillo's White Noise; Martin Amis's London Fields; essays by Donna Haraway and Edward Abbey; Carl Hiaasen's Double Whammy. We will also see the films Bladerunner, Never Cry Wolf, and Vernon, Florida. See the English Department's website at: www.english.upenn.edu for a description of the current offerings.
